# Git-Spice automatically adopts the active local gh-stack graph.

as 'Test <test@example.com>'
at '2026-08-06T12:30:00Z'

mkdir repo
cd repo
git init
git commit --allow-empty -m 'Initial commit'

gs branch create tracked -m tracked
gs trunk
git branch gh-one main
git branch gh-two main
git checkout gh-two

env GH_STACK_JSON={"schemaVersion":1,"repository":"","stacks":[{"trunk":{"branch":"main"},"branches":[{"branch":"gh-one","base":"","pullRequest":{"number":101,"id":"PR_one"}},{"branch":"gh-two","base":"","pullRequest":{"number":102,"id":"PR_two"}}]}]}
exec sh -c 'printf "%s\n" "$GH_STACK_JSON" > .git/gh-stack'

# No import or manual tracking command is needed.
gs log short
stderr 'gh-two.*#102'
stderr 'gh-one.*#101'
stderr 'main'
! stderr 'tracked'

# Git-Spice mutations update gh-stack state before returning.
exec sh -c 'printf "three\n" > third.txt'
git add third.txt
gs branch create gh-three -m 'gh-three'
exec sh -c 'tr -d "\\n " < .git/gh-stack'
stdout 'gh-one.*gh-two.*gh-three'
gs log short
stderr 'gh-one.*#101'
stderr 'gh-two.*#102'
stderr 'gh-three'

# The previous Git-Spice stack still exists, but only --all shows it.
gs log short --all
stderr 'tracked'
stderr 'gh-two'
stderr 'gh-one'

# If the two local sources disagree, fail instead of showing a stale stack.
git checkout tracked
! gs log short
stderr 'current branch "tracked" is tracked by Git-Spice but absent from gh-stack state'
